title: The wave of beer that flooded a London street
hook: A wave of beer once flooded a London street.
summary: In 1814 a slipped iron hoop on a giant brewery vat let loose a flood of beer in London, killing eight, and a court called it an act of God.
sources: Encyclopaedia Britannica / Wikipedia 'London Beer Flood': 17 October 1814, Meux's Horse Shoe Brewery, Tottenham Court Road; a vat burst after an iron hoop slipped; eight deaths.
Inquest ruled the deaths an 'act of God'; the brewery was not held liable and gained relief on excise duty (Wikipedia, Historic UK).

lines.text: A wave of beer once flooded a London street.
It was eighteen fourteen, at a brewery near Tottenham Court Road.
Inside stood a giant wooden vat, bound with heavy iron hoops.
That afternoon, one hoop slipped. Workers thought it was too small to matter.
An hour later, the vat burst, and the beer smashed into nearby homes.
lines.caps: An hour *later, | the vat *burst, | beer hit *homes

lines.text: Eight people died in the flood.
A court called it an act of God, so the brewery paid nothing.
One slipped ring drowned a street.

post.caption:
One loose iron hoop, and a whole street was swept away by beer.
Would you call it an act of God, or the brewery's fault?
